LHX.sentence: L3Harris bounced a bit this week and is actually leading the other defense contractors lately, though it's still well off its highs — unusual for a defense firm when military spending remains steady.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quiet, which is the whole point of this one — industrial gas goes out under long-term contracts, prices tick up a little each quarter, and investors drift toward it when the market gets nervous.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm — the stock isn't cheap, but its Azure cloud business keeps growing fast enough that nobody's worried, and there's no drama to report.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher has climbed back to its highs and is now outpacing its closest rival — the labs and drugmakers it supplies are buying steadily again.

CVX.sentence: Chevron barely moved, and while its profits look big right now, that's mostly because war near Iran has pushed oil far above normal — the company itself plans around a much lower oil price, so today's fat numbers are the oil price, not the business getting better.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow is down sharply from its high even though its peers are flat, which looks like sellers singling it out rather than a business problem — big companies and government agencies keep signing up for its workflow and AI-assistant tools on multi-year contracts.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore drifted flat today and is lagging the broader copper rally, so it's lagging a bit on metal prices that have been climbing.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta rose a little, and the thing that matters most is intact — the price it gets per ton of rock is still creeping up about 4%, even though a reported dip in average price is just an accounting quirk from acquisitions, not weakening demand.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA had a good day, but the Mexican peso is weakening — and since most of its sales are earned in pesos, that softens the value of its profits when converted back to dollars.

UBER.sentence: Uber climbed again, and people are still booking a lot more rides than before — well above the pace that would signal self-driving cars are eating into its business — so for now the robotaxi worry is about the future, not today's numbers.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk slipped a little and is trading for less than it would cost to replace its fleet of ships, which tends to be about as cheap as this shipping business gets.

MA.sentence: Mastercard is flat, but oddly it's trading slightly cheaper than Visa right now — rare, since it usually commands a premium — while people keep tapping their cards as much as ever.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical-robot company is down nearly a quarter from its high even though hospitals keep doing more operations right in line with its own forecast — so the fear in the stock isn't backed up by what the business is actually doing.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia fell again after Google's parent and Amazon showed they're now spending more on computing gear than their businesses earn and borrowing the rest — nothing changed at Nvidia itself, but those are exactly the customers who pay its bills, so whether they can keep spending is the whole question.
